# Oneway OS, every page in words

> The words of every page of Oneway OS on onewayos.com, read on 2026-10-20 from the pages themselves (tools/landing_static.py).

Oneway is a social network and a business platform in one: the Oneway App gives every person one profile, a For You feed, messages and a map of the people and places near them, and Oneway OS runs the businesses, communities and places behind them. It is in a closed beta, by invitation, in New York City and Long Island. Oneway, the Oneway App and Oneway OS are made only by Oneway Technologies LLC, of New York. We are not affiliated with oneway.tools, with the Oneway retail and self-checkout software at tryoneway.com, with the One Way services app, or with any other product that uses the name Oneway.

---

Business OS is $330 a month, set up by contact. Get Oneway OS today

Oneway OS runs a business, a community or a place: its page, website, posts, events and members for free, and with Business OS, the Systems of its industry, its team and the Brain, for $330 a month per Center.

What a Center is

A Center is whatever your place needs it to be.

A Center can be:

an information page for a place, a landmark or what locals know

a social profile with posts and followers, the way Instagram works

your business's website, on your own domain

a community's home, with members, groups, chat and events

a storefront that takes orders and bookings

the workspace your team runs the business from

Whichever it is, its page is a canvas its team lays out in Oneway OS, Popit by Popit.

System Store

Everything your Center needs.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

Systems bring industry and everyday capabilities into a Center. Explore what is available, then connect the tools that fit your operation.

For your kind of place

Not built yet: Consulting & Advisory, Agency Operations, Summer Camp Operations, Local Government, News Organization, Service Management, Short-Term Rental Operations, Dental Practice Operations, Mortgage Pipeline, Accounting Firm Client Management, Documents, Finance, Security & Access.

Install the Systems your place needs; each adds its tools to your Center and its Popits to the canvas.

Business OS vs. the stack

Seven apps, or one Center.

7 separate apps, or one Center on one login

Most businesses run on a pile of separate tools that never talk to each other. Business OS puts them in one Center, on one login.

Instead of On Business OS

A website builder Wix, Squarespace Your Center itself, as its website

A booking app Calendly, OpenTable Bookings and reservations, in the same Center people follow

An online store Shopify, Square Online A shop beside everything else the place does

A customer list HubSpot, Mailchimp Customers kept from every visit, order and message

A social media scheduler Hootsuite, Later Posts that go to the platforms you connect, from one place

A team chat and staff app Slack, Homebase Staff, roles and every message in one inbox

A link-in-bio page Linktree One Center that people follow, with everything on it

Add up your own stack: tick each tool you pay for and type what it costs you a month.

Your stack: $0 a month

Your stack costs a month more than Business OS.

Your numbers stay in your browser.

The names are examples of each kind of tool, and none of them has any affiliation with Oneway.

Compatibility & the Brain

Bring everything you use into one place.

On Business OS, the Brain sits under your Center. It connects the platforms and tools you already use, the Systems you install route back through it, and the whole operation moves as one.

Center →
Brain →
System Store →
Installed Systems →
Team · website · operations

How a Center grows

Start as a community. Grow into an operation.

4 stages, from a community to an enterprise

Stage 1
Community
Members, channels, events, and shared resources.

Stage 2
Connected
+ a public website, public intake, and Brain.

Stage 3
Operational
+ installed Systems and staff.

Stage 4
Enterprise
+ multiple Systems, departments, and advanced Brain.

## Business OS for Entertainment & Venues

Source: https://onewayos.com/os-business-entertainment

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Entertainment & Venues
Business OS

Entertainment & Venues.

Events with Going and Maybe, the people who come, the door on the night, and the work behind it.

Talk to us

Events

Found, answered and counted.

The Oneway App, with a sample Center.

People find the event on the Center's page in the Oneway App, say Going, Maybe or Not going, and see how many are going.

A draft until it is out
A draft is the team's alone until it is published. A cancelled event stays on the page and says so.

Spaces to book
A room, a court or a lane booked from the App. Where the venue confirms each booking, the guest is told it is a request before sending it.

System Store: Events and Reservations.

The door

Who is here, of who is coming.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

At the door the team sees the next events, how many are here of how many are coming, and checks each guest in with one press, or undoes it.

The people who come

Who follows, who has joined, who is going.

The Center's followers see its posts in their feeds, its members have joined it, and each event knows who is going.

The work

The work behind every night.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

Work orders on the venue's own things, in the order to do them.

Requests
Staff, members and guests with a booking report a problem, and Maintenance takes it on as a work order or declines it, saying why.

Inspections
A checklist the venue writes, run on a stage, a room or the whole place. An item that fails opens its own repair.

Preventive work
Upkeep that recurs opens its own work order before it is due.

Vendors
Work sent to a contractor, and what they said and what it cost when it came back.

Shifts
Each night's crew clocks in from their Workspace, and before payroll a manager fixes or excuses every late start and missed shift.

System Store: Maintenance, Asset Management and Scheduling.

Run your venue on Oneway OS.

## Business OS for Hospitality

Source: https://onewayos.com/os-business-hospitality

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Hospitality
Business OS

Hospitality.

Hotel operations, the guest's experience and the front office, in one Center.

Talk to us

Hotel Operations

The book, from the rate to the room.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

A hotel sells a room type, for a night, at a rate. The book keeps all three, and what is left to sell on every date.

Rooms and rates
Room types, rate plans and what is left to sell, by type and by date.

Holds and moves
A room taken out of sale for dates, with its reason, and a guest moved to another room in the house or before they arrive.

Group blocks
Rooms held for a group until its cut-off date, and the pick-up as its guests book.

Deposits and the city ledger
Deposits recorded as guests put them down, and the house accounts billed instead of the guest. Oneway records money and never moves it.

Pace
The nights ahead on the books, how fast they are coming in, and where last year stood at the same time.

Housekeeping and upkeep
A cleaned room sells only once a supervisor has inspected it. Upkeep follows use too, such as a boiler's run hours or an elevator's trips.

System Store: Hotel Operations, with Maintenance and Asset Management.

Guest Experience

Every guest, known across the property.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

What each department needs to know about a stay, the guest's own messages, and a program that rewards them for coming back.

Traces
A note about a guest's stay, for a department, on a day. The department sees it in its Workspace that day and marks it done.

Rewards
The hotel's own program: a tier earned within the program year is kept through the next, and the credits a guest spends lapse after months without activity. At a casino resort, the casino's own system keeps the points.

One inbox
Guests' messages arrive in the Center's one inbox.

A problem, reported once
A guest reports a problem in their room from the Oneway App, during the stay or up to 30 days after it. If the room already has work open, the report joins it, and the guest is told when it is fixed.

System Store: Rewards & Membership and Maintenance, beside Hotel Operations.

Front Office

The desk's day, and the numbers.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

Arrivals, the guests in the house and the ones leaving today, the night audit, and the figures every hotelier judges a property by.

The board
Who arrives, who is in the house and who is due out, with each room's state.

Check-in and the folio
The stay begins, the room becomes occupied, and a deposit held meets the folio every charge lands on.

The night audit
Each night's room charges and taxes posted to the folio, by the rules the property names.

The numbers
Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR from what the audit posted, beside the same night last year.

Charges to post
A check charged to a room by a connected point of sale waits for the desk, which posts it in one press. Nothing posts by itself.

The book you have today
A reservations export from the hotel system you use now, or a spreadsheet, brought in as this hotel's stays.

System Store: Reservations, with Hotel Operations.

Additional Hospitality Systems

The property's other systems, one intake.

What the hotel system, the points of sale, housekeeping and the valet report becomes one Center's events, one guest's timeline, and work for the person on shift.

One system at a time
Each is connected on its own, in Oneway OS's Integrations, and a system nobody has connected says exactly that.

One guest, on evidence
Two systems' guests are one guest only when the same card, the same address or the system's own guest id arrives from both. A name alone joins nothing.

Casino resorts
Oneway runs beside the casino management system. It reads it, writes nothing to it, and keeps no gaming money.

The casino's own day
The hosts' book of guests and their trips, the floor by area, and the pit's dealer rotation.

System Store: Casino Operations.

Run your property on Oneway OS.

## Business OS for Additional Industries

Source: https://onewayos.com/os-business-industries

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Additional Industries
Business OS

Additional Industries.

Rental property, and every kind of place a Center can be.

Talk to us

Rental property

The rent roll, unit by unit.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

Every unit leased, on notice or vacant, what is owed past its due date, and the leases coming to an end.

Units
Each unit named as the building names it, with its bedrooms and its asking rent.

Leases
The tenant, the rent, the deposit and the term: in force, on notice or ended. Two leases never overlap on one unit.

Statements
Each lease's rent, fees and credits, and the payments recorded against them. Oneway collects no rent.

Past due
What is owed, oldest first, aged 1⁠–⁠30, 31⁠–⁠60, 61⁠–⁠90 and over 90 days.

Renewals
The leases ending within 90 days, each renewed from where it shows.

Move-in and move-out
A checklist walked at each end of a lease. Once both are done, every item sound at move-in that failed at move-out is named, with both notes.

The owner's statement
A month of the property as its owner reads it: for each unit, what was charged and what was collected.

System Store: Property Management, with Maintenance for the work orders.

Every kind of place

A Center for every kind of place.

$0 Community Management, on Oneway OS

Museums and galleries, schools and clubs, churches and nonprofits, festivals, neighborhoods and cities.

A Center that is not a business
A community, a club, a festival or a city runs on the free Oneway OS and needs no Business OS.

Members
People join a Center's community from the Oneway App.

Events
What is on at the place, answered in the App.

System Store: Community Management, free on Oneway OS. Events, Reservations and Scheduling come with Business OS.

Give your place a Center.

## Business OS for Restaurants

Source: https://onewayos.com/os-business-restaurants

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Restaurants
Business OS

Restaurants.

The floor and the kitchen, run from Oneway OS.

Talk to us

The floor

Every table, and who is at it.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

The host sees each table with its seats and its section, the party at it, and how long they have been there.

Tables and sections
Each table is one of the restaurant's own things: its number, its seats and its section.

Every seating
A walk-in, a party from the waitlist or a booking that has arrived, seated and then cleared for the next party.

Bookings due
The bookings due at your tables over the next twelve hours, each seated in one press.

Turn times
The day's turn times, with its covers and its parties.

The table that fits
For a party waiting, the floor names an open table that seats them and is not held for a booking before they would leave. The host still chooses.

Returning guests
A guest who has let places recognize them is named as returning, at the table and in the line.

System Store: Restaurant Operations, with Reservations for the bookings.

The waitlist

The line, on the guest's phone too.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

Who is waiting, how many, the quote they were given and how long they have waited, and which parties are past their quote.

Join from the App
A guest joins the waitlist from the restaurant's page in the Oneway App and follows their own place in line.

Ready
When the host says a table is ready, a guest who joined from the App is told there at once. Anyone else, the host calls.

The kitchen

The 86 board.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

What the kitchen is out of today, who said so and when, and back on with one press.

Point of sale

Your point of sale stays.

Once it is connected, a check opened or closed at a table shows on the floor. Oneway takes no payment.

Of a closed check, Oneway keeps its totals, and never the tips, the payment or what was ordered.

System Store

Add what the restaurant needs.

5 Systems a restaurant starts with

A restaurant can start with these five.

Restaurant Operations
The floor, the waitlist and the 86 board.

Reservations
A party books a table from the Oneway App for as many as it seats, and a time already taken says when the table is next free.

Scheduling
Shifts for the floor and the kitchen, flagged when one would leave someone less than eight hours' rest or take their week past 40 hours. Someone who cannot work a shift offers it, and a manager approves whoever takes it.

Maintenance
Repairs on the kitchen's own equipment, and when one piece keeps breaking, its failures read as one incident with what fixed it last time.

Rewards & Membership
A diner's card, opened by their member number, with what they spend on dining posted to it and credits redeemed from it.

Run your restaurant on Oneway OS.
Talk to us Business OS

Oneway Business OS.

The full business operating system: the Brain, Systems, Agents, Cross Projection and operational intelligence.

Industries

Start with your industry.

Oneway OS, with sample records.

Each page shows what Business OS runs for that kind of place, and the Systems it starts with.

Restaurants
Seating the floor, a waitlist guests follow on their phones, and what the kitchen has run out of.

Hospitality
Rooms sold by type and rate, the front desk through its night audit, and casino resorts beside their own systems.

Entertainment & Venues
Who is coming to each event, checking them in as they arrive, and keeping the venue in repair.

Additional Industries
Leases and what tenants owe, for rental property, and a Center for a museum, a school, a club or a city.

What it carries

The business layer of a Center.

$330 a month for one Center on Business OS

Everything a free Center has, and the parts a business runs on.

Systems
Each industry's tools, picked in the System Store and installed into the Center.

The Brain
The memory of the whole operation.

Cross Projection
Where the business's own website or its map entry shows other hours or another phone number than its record, the Brain sets the two side by side for someone to choose. The choice is written once, and every page that reads the record shows it.

Agents
Not built yet.

Bring your business to Oneway OS.

## Oneway Asset Management

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/asset-management

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Asset Management
Core System

Asset Management.

Asset Management tracks every physical thing your business owns: where it is, who has it, what it costs, and the upkeep that keeps it running.

The base every physical System runs on: Hotel Operations, Restaurant Operations, Property Management, HVAC and more.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta.

Talk to us

Asset Management in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The register

Anything, in your own words.

Every thing, one register
Found by words, tag, code, kind, place or state; changed many at a time.

Where it stands
Places inside places, and things inside things; moving one moves what it holds.

A QR code for each
Printed in house; scanning it opens the thing in the OS.

Lent and returned
Checked out to a person until a day, never twice; back with its condition.

Bought and warranted
Price, supplier, warranty and useful life; warranties ending in 90 days listed.

A guided audit
Walked place by place, with what was not found.

The register's report, the map of every thing by place, and the work each department does.

Maintenance

Kept working, and the cost known.

Work orders
Handed to whoever is on the clock with the fewest open, who is told on their phone.

Closed with the proof
Parts, cost, hours and pictures of the fix, on the thing's own record.

Last time this happened
The next person sees what fixed it before, picture and all.

Preventive work that opens itself
Every so many days, or by a meter's reading; on time, late and overdue said.

Reported once
Guests, members and staff report from the App and are told when it is fixed.

Sensors feeding meters
A meter read from the equipment itself, through its sensors feed.

Cost and condition

Repair it or replace it.

Condition and state, apart
Working, degraded or failed, and in or out of service; out of order leaves what can be sold.

Downtime, every span
Hours down in the last 90 days and in all, from the thing's own history.

Reliability
Mean time between failures and to repair, and the least reliable things.

Cost of ownership
Price plus every repair, book value, and when replacing is worth weighing.

A history nobody rewrites
Every change, who, when and why.

Scheduled reports
The report sent to the owners in Oneway on its day, and the register as a sheet.

The base

One physical world under every System.

A hotel's rooms, a casino's machines and a customer's furnace are all assets. Each industry System adds its own kinds of things and its own work; the condition, history and upkeep are the same everywhere.

Each industry has its own System
Its own install, screens and acts, on these assets.

Installed together
Installing Hotel Operations installs Asset Management, Reservations and Maintenance with it.

How it works

A thing, and everything that happens to it.

Add it
By hand, from a spreadsheet or a QR label.

Use it
Booked, lent, sold or worked on.

Keep it working
Work orders and preventive upkeep on the thing.

Know its cost
Downtime, repairs and the case to replace it.

Who it is for

Every place that owns things.

Hotels and resorts
Rooms, elevators, kitchens and plant.

Venues and casinos
Machines, tables and the floor.

Property managers
Units and what is inside them.

Gyms, schools and offices
Equipment, rooms and vehicles.

Comes with these Systems

Casino Operations System
Oneway Events
Oneway Hotel Operations
Oneway Inventory Management
Oneway Maintenance
Property Management System
Restaurant Operations System

At a glance

Oneway Asset Management, in facts.

What it is Asset Management tracks every physical thing your business owns: where it is, who has it, what it costs, and the upkeep that keeps it running.
Part of Oneway OS, as a core system of Business OS.
Comes with Casino Operations System, Events, Hotel Operations System, Inventory Management, Maintenance, Property Management System, Restaurant Operations System.
Where it runs In Oneway OS, in a web browser on a computer or a phone.
Price Part of Business OS: $330 a month for one Center, set up by contact. Oneway OS alone is free.
Status In the Closed Selective Server Beta, by invitation, in New York City and Long Island.
Made by Oneway Technologies LLC, New York.

Know every thing you own.

## Oneway Communications

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/communications

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Communications
Module

Communications.

Oneway Communications puts every message to your business in one shared inbox, answers the routine ones by rule, and tells your team what it needs to know.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Communications in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The inbox

Every conversation, one inbox.

One shared inbox
Every conversation people start with the business in the Oneway App.

Who has the line
Assigned to a person, escalated with a reason, concluded with its outcome.

Saved replies
The business's own answers, by name, one press away.

Automatic replies
A greeting, an away message and the business's own questions, sent by rule.

Other channels
SMS, WhatsApp, email, Instagram and Messenger in the same inbox.
Planned

Translation
A message read and answered in the guest's language.
Planned

Notes to the team, and who they reached.

The team

What the team needs to know, once.

Tell the team
A note to everyone, or to one department, and who it reached.

In each person's day
A line handed to someone reaches their day in the Oneway App.

A message to every guest in the house
One message to everyone staying, or to a group.
Planned

Messages scheduled across a stay
Before arrival, during and after, sent on their day.
Planned

The difference

The inbox knows the customer.

An inbox tool sees messages. Here each line sits beside the customer's bookings and history.

Beside the CRM
Who is writing, and what they have booked, next to what they wrote.

Your rules, your words
Automatic replies say only what the business wrote.

One team
Assigned to the people the Center's roles name.

How it works

From a message to an answer.

It arrives
In one inbox, from the App.

Routine is answered
By the business's own rules.

The rest is handed on
To a person, told in their day.

It is concluded
With its outcome, kept.

Who it is for

Any business people write to.

Hotels
Guests before, during and after a stay.

Restaurants
Bookings, questions and parties.

Venues
Tickets, guest lists and the night.

Communities
Members and their questions.

At a glance

Oneway Communications, in facts.

What it is Oneway Communications puts every message to your business in one shared inbox, answers the routine ones by rule, and tells your team what it needs to know.
Part of Oneway OS, as a module of Business OS.
Where it runs In Oneway OS, in a web browser on a computer or a phone.
Price Part of Business OS: $330 a month for one Center, set up by contact. Oneway OS alone is free.
Status In the Closed Selective Server Beta, by invitation, in New York City and Long Island.
Made by Oneway Technologies LLC, New York.

## Oneway CRM

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/crm

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Oneway CRM
Core System

Oneway CRM.

Oneway CRM keeps every customer's whole story, from their real bookings, visits and messages, so your team knows who they are and what to do next.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Oneway CRM in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The record

One customer, one story.

Bookings, stays, orders, posts and messages land on the same record, so nobody types a history in.

A timeline per customer
Notes, deals and their moves, stays, orders paid, rewards and messages, newest first.

Tags, an owner and your own fields
Words, numbers, dates and lists of your own, filtered and exported.

Consent, said once
Email, texts and calls each agreed or refused. Do-not-contact stops every campaign and audience.

Joined on evidence
Two records become one only on a confirmed address or id, never on a name.

Duplicates merged
Found by email, phone or name and merged by an owner, with every deal carried over.

Auto-tags by rule
Regulars and big spenders tagged from what they did.
Planned

Each customer's record: the timeline, the deals, the follow-ups and their consent.

Pipeline

From the first message to the signed deal.

Deals at six stages, each with its chance to close and what it is worth.

Deals and stages
Lead, qualified, proposal, negotiation, won and lost, with value and weighted value.

Won and lost, with why
The last 90 days' win rate, the reasons deals were lost, each owner's share.

Follow-ups that land
A due day and hour, handed to a person who is told, on their own Workspace.

Leads from your own book
People who booked with their account and are not on your list, made customers in one press.

Your own stages and several pipelines
Stages named your way, a pipeline per kind of sale.
Planned

A reminder at the hour
A follow-up that rings when it is due.
Planned

Lists and data

Your customers, yours to move.

Saved lists that keep up
By tag, owner, company, stage, consent or words, counted again every time.

Search everything
Names, addresses, phones, companies, tags and notes.

Import and export
A CSV in, each refused row named; every column out, a list or a filter at a time.

The report
Pipeline by stage, won and lost, follow-ups open, overdue and done.

Email from the CRM
Sequences, templates and tracking.
Planned

Web forms
Your site's forms making contacts.
Planned

The difference

A CRM that does not need feeding.

Most CRMs are only as good as what someone types in. Oneway CRM is fed by the business itself.

Part of the business
Reservations, rewards, orders and messages write to the same customer. Nothing to sync.

Their own profile, live
A customer on Oneway keeps their name and face current themselves.

Private by default
Staff see customers only when their role works with them. Strangers see nothing.

How it works

From what happened to who to call.

Something happens
A booking, a visit, an order or a message.

It finds its customer
On evidence: the same address or id.

The record moves
Its story, its deals and its tags.

The team acts
Follow-ups due land on the right person.

Who it is for

Any business people come back to.

Hotels and resorts
Repeat guests known before they arrive.

Restaurants
Regulars, their table and their preferences.

Services and practices
Clients and the next appointment owed.

Venues and clubs
Members, groups and their bookings.

Comes with these Systems

Casino Operations System
Oneway Hotel Operations
Restaurant Operations System

At a glance

Oneway CRM, in facts.

What it is Oneway CRM keeps every customer's whole story, from their real bookings, visits and messages, so your team knows who they are and what to do next.

Hotel Operations.

Hotel Operations runs a hotel's rooms, rates and guests from one place, from the booking and the front desk to the night audit and housekeeping.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Hotel Operations in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The book

From the rate to the room.

Stays
Booked by room and dates; what is left to sell, by type and night.

Rates
A rate ladder per room type; a type closed to sale on chosen dates.

Group blocks
Rooms held to a cut-off, released after, tied to the group's event.

Taxes and terms
The room taxes a stay is charged, and the registration card's words.

The book you have today
An export from your current system, brought in as stays.

Online travel agencies
Rooms and rates sent to booking sites, bookings back.
Planned

The nights ahead on the books, and what each department does next.

Front desk

The desk's whole day.

Arrivals, in house, due out
Every room's state beside the guests.

Check in, check out, move
Deposits recorded, rooms moved before or during the stay.

Charges
Posted by the desk, or waiting from the point of sale for one press.

The night audit
Each night's room charges and taxes, posted by your rules.

The numbers
Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR beside the same night last year.

Folios and accounts

Every charge, and who pays it.

Oneway records money and never moves it.

Routing
A stay's charges sent to a house account or another folio.

House accounts
Billed as numbered invoices, paid oldest first, closed.

Disputes and write-offs
Each with who and why.

Split a bill by payer
Separate windows on one folio.
Planned

Recurring and batch charges
A charge that repeats, or one charge to many accounts.
Planned

Housekeeping

Clean, inspected, and known.

Room status from a phone
Dirty, cleaned, inspected, ready; a room sells only once inspected.

Rooms to clean
Each assigned to a person, on their phone.

Out of order
Taken out of sale with its reason, and returned to service.

Traces
A note about a stay for a department on a day, marked done.

Runs on Asset Management

Every room is an asset.

Hotel Operations is its own System, with its own install, screens and acts. Its rooms are assets, so condition, history and upkeep are the same records engineering works on.

Out of order is not out of service
Out of order leaves what can be sold; out of service stays in the count.

Inventory Management.

Oneway Inventory tracks stock levels, orders, sales and deliveries across your supply chain, so your business has the right amount of goods in the right place at the right time.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Inventory Management in Oneway OS, with sample records.

Stock levels

The right amount, in every place.

Items, packs and variants
A unit, pack sizes, a SKU and a barcode; sizes and colours each counted on their own.

By place and by shelf
Stock where it actually sits, in every place the business keeps it.

Counts
A whole place or item by item; the difference shown at once, booked by an owner.

Waste with a reason
Spoiled, damaged, expired, lost or used in house, each in dollars.

One history
Every change kept for good; on hand is never typed over.

Lots and expiry
Each delivery's lot and the day it expires.
Planned

Every item is one of the business's things: on the map by place, with its own history.

Orders and deliveries

Ordered before it runs out, received as it comes.

A demand forecast
When each item will run out at today's pace, and when to order.

Orders drafted for you
What is low, onto its supplier's order, filled to par and rounded to the pack.

Approved and on its way
An owner approves the order and marks it sent; open orders are listed until they arrive.

Deliveries received
Received in part or in full, at the invoice's cost; what never came is said.

Suppliers measured
Their stated lead time beside the real one, fill rate and on-time count.

The day each delivery is expected, and the ones that are late.

A purchase order by email or PDF.

What a dish uses, and what it costs to make.
Planned

One supply chain, every place in it.

Moved between places
From one place and shelf to another, both halves in one step.

Property to property
Sent to another property of the same business, found there by its SKU.

Every property at once
On hand, low items and open orders for each property, side by side.

Parts on a work order
Their cost lands on the repair, and on the thing it fixed.

Suggested transfers
Stock one property has to spare, offered where another runs low.
Planned

The difference

One stock for the whole business.

Kitchen tools count the kitchen; maintenance tools count parts. Here every department writes to one history.

Tied to the work
A part used on a repair is on that repair, and on the thing it fixed.

Tied to the customer
What is out reaches the Shop and the App, not only the storeroom.

Every item is a thing you own
Stock lives in Asset Management's register, on the same map.

How it works

A movement, every time.

It is ordered
Before it runs out, from its supplier, approved by an owner.

It arrives
Received against its order, at the invoice's cost.

It is kept
On a shelf in a place, counted when you count, moved where it is needed.

It is sold or used
By a sale, a department or a repair, and ordered again.

Anyone who keeps things on a shelf.

Hotels
Linen, amenities and engineering's parts.

Restaurants and bars
Food and drink, counted and costed.

Shops
What is for sale, and what is left.

Service companies
The parts every truck carries.

Maintenance.

Oneway Maintenance turns every problem anyone reports into a work order, keeps preventive upkeep on schedule, and shows what each repair cost.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta.

Talk to us

Maintenance in Oneway OS, with sample records.

Work orders

Every problem, one work order.

Open, hand on, close
Opened, assigned and told, closed with what fixed it, its cost, parts, hours and pictures.

How urgent
Low, medium or high, ranked in the queue.

On hold
Waiting on a part or a vendor, said, never lost as in progress.

The board
To do, started and on hold, moved by hand.

Requests
Reported from the Oneway App by guests, members and staff, with a picture, each answer told.

Steps on the job
A checklist's steps on the work order, ticked, and Done refused while one is left.

The work as a board: to do, started, on hold.

Upkeep

Before it breaks.

Preventive by time
Every so many days, with a lead, never piling up; on-time compliance said.

Preventive by meter
Every so many hours or uses, read by a person or by the equipment's sensor.

Inspections
A checklist walked and finished, lease inspections included.

Incidents
One thing that keeps failing, read as one incident with what fixed it last time.

Who does it

The right hands, at the right cost.

The technician's phone
Their work, Start and Done, what fixed it, hours and pictures, offline steps kept.

Vendors
Sent with a not-to-exceed, accepted or declined, done with its cost.

Parts from Inventory
Parts used come off the shelf, their cost on the repair.

Escalation
Work nobody takes is raised, by rules the Center sets.

Hours from the clock
Done fills the hours from its Start, to the quarter hour, unless hours are said.

The difference

Maintenance on the same map as everything.

A maintenance app keeps its own list of equipment. Here work lands on the Center's own things.

Every thing is a thing you own
Work lands on Asset Management's register: downtime and cost of ownership per thing.

Parts from Inventory
The shelf and the repair are one history.

From reported to fixed.

From the App, the desk or a schedule.

Assigned
To a person or a vendor, told.

Done
What fixed it, the parts, the hours and the cost.

Learned
Downtime and repeat failures, per thing.

Anyone who keeps a building running.

Units and the tenants' requests.

Restaurants
The kitchen's equipment.

Venues and clubs
Everything the night depends on.

## Oneway Reservations

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/reservations

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Reservations
Module

Reservations.

Oneway Reservations lets people book the things your place offers, a room, a table, a court or a space, from the Oneway App, and runs the book from confirmation to check-out.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Reservations in Oneway OS, with sample records.

What is booked

Anything your place offers, bookable.

Bookable things
A room, a table, a court, a boat or a space: any of the Center's things takes bookings.

Its hours
When each one takes bookings, day by day.

Availability
What is free and when, read before anyone books.

A grid across things
The day drawn as a timeline across every bookable thing.
Planned

What can be booked, with its hours and its rules.

Booking

Booked from the App, kept in one book.

Booked from the App
A person books from the Center's page and sees their bookings in their own.

Cancelled by the guest
A guest cancels their own booking, and the time is free again.

The desk's book
The day's bookings, waiting on you and from today on.

Confirm, check in, check out
The desk moves each booking through its day.

Deposits and cards on file
A deposit taken when the booking is made.
Planned

Filling the time

Nothing booked is an opportunity.

Idle things
Every bookable thing with nothing booked in the coming days, said.

Offered as a space
An idle thing proposed as a space opportunity, published by its owner.

Shown everywhere
The same booking facts shaped for a Popit, a Center page, an event and the web.

The difference

Booked where people already are.

A booking widget waits on a website. Here the Center's page in the App is where people book.

Every thing is a thing you own
Bookable things live in Asset Management's register.

One book for the desk
Rooms, tables and courts in one place.

Idle time said
What nobody booked is proposed as something to offer.

How it works

From a free hour to a full one.

Make it bookable
Choose a thing and its hours.

People book
From the Center's page in the Oneway App.

The desk runs the day
Confirm, check in, check out.

Idle time offered
What nobody booked becomes an offer.

Who it is for

Anywhere people book a time.

Hotels and resorts
Rooms, the spa, cabanas and courts.

Restaurants
Tables and private rooms.

Clubs and venues
Courts, lanes and rooms.

Communities
Shared spaces members book.

Comes with these Systems

Casino Operations System
Oneway Events
Oneway Hotel Operations
Property Management System
Restaurant Operations System

At a glance

Oneway Reservations, in facts.

What it is Oneway Reservations lets people book the things your place offers, a room, a table, a court or a space, from the Oneway App, and runs the book from confirmation to check-out.
Part of Oneway OS, as a module of Business OS.
Comes with Casino Operations System, Events, Hotel Operations System, Property Management System, Restaurant Operations System.
Where it runs In Oneway OS, in a web browser on a computer or a phone.
Price Part of Business OS: $330 a month for one Center, set up by contact. Oneway OS alone is free.
Status In the Closed Selective Server Beta, by invitation, in New York City and Long Island.
Made by Oneway Technologies LLC, New York.

Every hour, bookable.

## Oneway Rewards

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/rewards

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Rewards & Membership
Module

Rewards & Membership.

Oneway Rewards runs your loyalty program: members earn credits for what they do at your place, move up tiers, and redeem what they have earned.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Rewards & Membership in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The program

Your program, your rules.

Tiers and benefits
Each tier named, the credits it takes, and what it gives.

Earned for activity
Credits posted for a stay, a meal or a visit.

Redeemed
Credits spent at the place, kept on the card.

Lapsing credits
Credits that expire after the program's months, by a run the owner checks first.

Adjusted with a reason
A card corrected, the reason kept.

The program's tiers, and its members.

Members

Every member, one card.

Enrolled anywhere
From a customer record, a Oneway person or a name, or joined in the App.

Their card in the App
Each member reads their own card, and chooses what they share.

Cards from other programs
A member links the card they already hold; a provider's export confirms it.

Recognized elsewhere
Whose standing this Center honours, and as what.

Offers to a tier
An offer addressed to members of one tier.
Planned

The difference

A card people already carry.

A loyalty app is one more app to download. Here the card lives in the Oneway App members already use.

In the App
The member's card, beside the place's page.

Their choice
What a member shares with the place, they decide.

Other programs welcome
A card from another program, linked, never copied.

How it works

From a visit to a reward.

Enrol
At the desk, from the CRM, or in the App.

Earn
Credits for what members do.

Rise
Tiers with their benefits.

Redeem
Credits spent at the place.

Who it is for

Any place people come back to.

Hotels and resorts
Nights, upgrades and the spa.

Restaurants and bars
Meals and the regulars.

Casinos
Play and comps, beside the casino's own program.

Clubs
Members and their standing.

Comes with these Systems

Casino Operations System

At a glance

Oneway Rewards, in facts.

What it is Oneway Rewards runs your loyalty program: members earn credits for what they do at your place, move up tiers, and redeem what they have earned.
Part of Oneway OS, as a module of Business OS.
Comes with Casino Operations System.
Where it runs In Oneway OS, in a web browser on a computer or a phone.
Price Part of Business OS: $330 a month for one Center, set up by contact. Oneway OS alone is free.
Status In the Closed Selective Server Beta, by invitation, in New York City and Long Island.
Made by Oneway Technologies LLC, New York.

Give them a reason to come back.

## Oneway Scheduling

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/scheduling

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Scheduling
Module

Scheduling.

Oneway Scheduling builds your team's week of shifts, lets people claim, swap and take time off, and keeps the clock and the cost of every hour.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Scheduling in Oneway OS, with sample records.

The week

A week of shifts, published once.

Shifts by role
Each shift with its hours and role, edited until the week is published.

Open shifts
A shift nobody has yet, claimed by someone who can take it.

Publish the week
The team reads its week once it is published, each person their own.

Availability
Each person says when they can work.

Copy last week
A week's shifts copied into the next as drafts, never twice.

Shift reminders
A reminder before each published shift.
Planned

The week, shift by shift: who has it, or nobody yet.

The team

Swaps and time off, decided by a manager.

Offer and swap
A shift offered to the team, taken or swapped, the change decided once.

Time off
Asked for, decided, and kept out of the schedule.

Notes on the week
A note to the team, and who has seen it.

Who is on
Everyone on a shift, from the shift itself.

Time and cost

Every hour clocked, and what it cost.

The time clock
Clocked in and out; a punch corrected or voided, with who did it.

Timesheets approved
The week's hours approved by a manager.

Pay rates
An hourly rate per person from the day it starts, kept by an owner.

Labour against sales
The day's and the week's labour cost, and its share of sales.

Staffing from the book
How many people a day's bookings and events need, beside who is scheduled.

Timesheets out for payroll
Hours, rate and cost per person, as a sheet for the payroll provider.
Planned

Clock-in at the place
A clock-in only where the work is.
Planned

The difference

The schedule knows the work.

A scheduling app knows shifts. Here the week sits beside the bookings, events and sales it serves.

From the book
The staffing need is read from the day's bookings and events.

Against the sales
Labour is weighed against the sales the Center's points of sale report.

One team
The same people the Center's roles and permits name, never a second list.

How it works

A week, every week.

Build the week
Shifts by role, with the open ones left open.

Publish it
Everyone reads their own week.

The team settles it
Claims, swaps and time off, decided by a manager.

Clock and cost
Hours clocked, approved, and weighed against sales.

Who it is for

Any team that works in shifts.

Hotels
The desk, housekeeping and engineering around the clock.

Restaurants and bars
The floor and the kitchen, against the night's sales.

Venues
The crew each event needs.

Shops and services
Opening hours covered, every day.

At a glance

Oneway Scheduling, in facts.

What it is Oneway Scheduling builds your team's week of shifts, lets people claim, swap and take time off, and keeps the clock and the cost of every hour.
Part of Oneway OS, as a module of Business OS.
Where it runs In Oneway OS, in a web browser on a computer or a phone.
Price Part of Business OS: $330 a month for one Center, set up by contact. Oneway OS alone is free.
Status In the Closed Selective Server Beta, by invitation, in New York City and Long Island.
Made by Oneway Technologies LLC, New York.

The week, built and covered.

## Oneway Team

Source: https://onewayos.com/systems/team

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Oneway OS › Business OS › Team
Module

Team.

Oneway Team keeps who works at your business, what each of them may see and do, and every permit and license before it lapses.

Part of Business OS, by contact, in the Closed Selective Server Beta. What is still being built is marked Planned.

Talk to us

Team in Oneway OS, with sample records.

Roles

Each person sees their own work.

Custom roles
A role named by the business, with the Systems, departments and acts it may use.

Assigned
Each person given a role, and refused outside it, in words.

Work apart from life
Work for a Center kept apart from a person's own activity.

Onboarding checklists
A new hire's first steps, ticked.
Planned

Permits and licenses, each with the day it expires.

Permits

Nothing lapses unnoticed.

Permits and licenses
Each with its issuer, holder, number and expiry.

Reminded before it lapses
Told once, ahead of the day.

An expired one, said
On the OS's Home, until it is renewed.

Their time

Shifts and hours, with Scheduling.

Their week
Each person's shifts, time off and the clock, from Scheduling.

Payroll
Pay run and paid through a payroll provider.
Planned

The difference

One person, one identity.

An HR tool keeps its own copy of each person. Here each one is the same person across the platform.

Their own account
One Oneway account, a work identity kept apart.

Roles that refuse
Outside their role, an act is refused in words.

The same team everywhere
Scheduling, Maintenance and the inbox read the same people.

How it works

From a hire to a team.

Invite them
To the Center, with a role.

They see their work
Only what their role allows.

Keep the papers
Permits and licenses, reminded.

Run the week
With Scheduling.

Who it is for

Any business with a team.

Hotels
Every department, its own view.

Restaurants
Front and back of house.

Venues
The crew and its licenses.

Service companies
Technicians and their certifications.

At a glance

Oneway Team, in facts.

What it is Oneway Team keeps who works at your business, what each of them may see and do, and every permit and license before it lapses.
Part of Oneway OS, as a module of Business OS.
Where it runs In Oneway OS, in a web browser on a computer or a phone.
Price Part of Business OS: $330 a month for one Center, set up by contact. Oneway OS alone is free.
Status In the Closed Selective Server Beta, by invitation, in New York City and Long Island.
Made by Oneway Technologies LLC, New York.

The right people, with the right access.
